column5: reads, and comes back as ...--5?2Kdo--... : KDO is silently respelled Kdo. Both Hept residues come back superclass=Unknown, isSubstituent=false

column1: # What #255 says is happening, and is not. The issue reads "the first Heptose residue becomes a
# Substituent of the KDO residue". Parsed from the string above, neither Hept is a substituent in the
# model - both are plain unknown saccharides. Whatever makes one look like a substituent happens in
# placement or drawing, not in the parser, and a fix aimed at the parser will miss it.
# What the dictionaries actually offer for a heptose:
#   residue_types:100-101        L-gro-D-manHep, D-gro-D-manHep        superclass Unknown
#   residue_types:105            %Hep                                  commented out - % is this
#                                                                      file's comment marker, so the
#                                                                      generic heptose row is off
#   non_symbolic_residue_types   thirteen more X-gro-Y-zzzHep          superclass Unknown
#   (nowhere)                    Hept                                  the spelling GlycoWorkbench
#                                                                      writes; created on the fly by
#                                                                      createUnknown
#   residue_styles_cfg:71        Hept -> heptagon                      never reached: getStyle keys
#   residue_styles_cfgbw:59      Hept -> heptagon                      on the type NAME, and no
#                                                                      residue is named Hept
#   residue_styles_snfg          (no heptose row)                      so it falls back to the
#                                                                      superclass row, Unknown ->
#                                                                      hexagon, which is #254/#248
# So heptose fails in all three directions at once: the generic row is disabled, the fifteen specific
# rows cannot survive a GWS round trip, and the spelling another program writes is in no dictionary.
# One grammar change (docs/gws-format.md 1.3) fixes the third column; the first two are dictionary
# edits and want a chemistry opinion, not a code change.
